children: Domestic markets are likely to open on flat to positive note, after a long break, on Tuesday. Gift Nifty at 23,540 signals a gain of about 50 points. However, analysts expect the market to remain volatile due to rising inflation and renewed pressure in West Asia.

“India’s headline CPI inflation rose to 4.82% in August 2026 from 4.45% in July, a fourth straight monthly increase, though still within the RBI’s tolerance band. “Food inflation climbed to 5.95%, driven by sharp spikes in onion (+48.3%), garlic (+43.6%) and ginger (+73.8%), even as tomato and potato stayed in deep deflation, pointing to volatile vegetable dynamics rather than a broad-based food shock. Core inflation, excluding food and fuel, is estimated near 4.3%, kept elevated by gold and silver prices amid geopolitical risk aversion and firm crude-linked transport costs,” said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.

Going forward, we expect headline inflation to stay range-bound near 4.5-5.0%, with food the key swing factor amid uneven monsoon and El Niño-related uncertainty. The main risk is that high wholesale food and input costs eventually push up retail prices, alongside any rise in crude oil or fresh volatility in vegetable prices, he said.

Kruti Shah, quant analyst, Equirus Securities, said  Globally, higher crude oil prices, a volatile DXY and weakness in the S&P 500 and rising yield continue to weigh on risk sentiment. “However, the current correction appears driven more by low volumes & positioning , suggesting downside may become increasingly limited as shorts build,” she said.

Sector leadership remains selective. IT continues to face pressure, while weakness has started to emerge in the broader midcap universe as market breadth cools from elevated levels. In contrast, CPSE stocks are attracting delivery-based buying, and metals remain supported by strength in base metals, with copper trading at record highs.
There are indications of FPI flows again turning negative after the positive flows in July and August.

VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Ltd, said,NSDL data up to September 12 shows FPI outflows of Rs 14474 crores via selling through the exchanges. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market has been continuing in September also as per early indications. FPI investment through the primary market up to 12th September stood at Rs 1336 crores taking the total investment through the primary market this year to Rs 47183 crores. This partly explains the ongoing boom in the primary market despite the tepid performance of the secondary market, he said.
Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, said  the immediate focus will be on U.S. inflation and the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.

“The September 15–16 FOMC meeting will therefore be the week’s principal global catalyst. A rate hike accompanied by hawkish economic projections could strengthen the dollar, tighten global financial conditions and place further pressure on emerging-market equities, foreign flows and the rupee. Conversely, an unchanged policy rate—or a hike accompanied by balanced forward guidance—could trigger a relief rally if investors interpret the outcome as less restrictive than feared. The Bank of England and Bank of Japan will add to the central-bank focus later in the week, with their policy decisions due on September 17 and September 17–18, respectively,” he said.

For India, crude oil remains the most immediate external risk. Brent crude settled at $104.61 a barrel after briefly approaching $110, leaving prices well above levels that would be considered comfortable for an import-dependent economy. Any renewed rise in crude, particularly if disruptions to Middle East oil flows intensify, could add to inflationary pressures, widen the import bill, weigh on the rupee and squeeze corporate margins. Domestic data, including WPI inflation and trade figures, will provide additional clues on how much of that pressure is filtering into the economy.

title: Positive opening seen for domestic markets amid headwinds
